answer: Lineage-Seal Attestation. Each identity must publish a signed derivation record embedding a unique kernel value tied to its operator's prior deployments. Duplication is detected when two records share a kernel but claim disjoint parents, exposing the fork. A public ridge of recent lineage hashes anchors each new record, forcing attackers to rebuild history per fake identity. The cost is one full derivation chain — compute plus a sustained dune of timestamped entries — per duplicate, making mass sybils linear-cost and detectable.
